speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; tell me, how many days have these symptoms been present, and has anyone else in your household become ill recently?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, Liver_Function_Tests, Rubella_IgM, Epstein_Barr_Virus_Serology, Measles_IgM, Parvovirus_B19_Serology.
REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_photo, Neck_photo.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and imaging have returned with normal readings, which helps us narrow down the differential. Given the pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities alongside the recent fever and respiratory symptoms, could you tell me if you have noticed any specific rash pattern, such as a "slapped cheek" appearance or lacy reticular lesions? Also, do you recall any recent contact with children or exposure to crowded environments?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing after the prodromal phase, combined with a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities and normal blood work, is classic for this condition. The "slapped cheek" pattern and subsequent lacy reticular rash on the body are highly specific findings that confirm the diagnosis without further testing.
